parsedContent.method: To evaluate a firm's net-working capital position, we need to consider the conflict between liquidity and profitability objectives. The current ratio (Current Assets / Current Liabilities) and the quick ratio (Quick Assets / Current Liabilities) are used to assess liquidity, while the return on assets (Net Income / Total Assets) and return on equity (Net Income / Total Equity) are used to assess profitability. Each formula is weighted by the specific components of the balance sheet and income statement it divides by.
keyPoints: Liquidity refers to a firm's ability to meet its short-term obligations
Profitability refers to a firm's ability to generate earnings
The current ratio and quick ratio are used to assess liquidity
The return on assets and return on equity are used to assess profitability
A trade-off exists between liquidity and profitability, as increasing liquidity may decrease profitability and vice versa
